title: 1986 AHSME Problem 11
statement: In \(\triangle ABC,\) \(AB=13,\) \(BC=14\) and \(CA=15.\) Also, \(M\) is the midpoint of side \(AB\) and \(H\) is the foot of the altitude from \(A\) to \(BC.\) The length of \(HM\) is

solutions.text:
Triangle \(AHB\) is right at \(H,\) and \(M\) is the midpoint of its hypotenuse \(AB.\) The midpoint of a right triangle’s hypotenuse is equidistant from all three vertices, so \[ HM=\frac{AB}{2}=\frac{13}{2}=6.5. \]

Thus the correct answer is B.
hints: Recall the distance from the midpoint of a right triangle’s hypotenuse to each vertex
